saw_lines: Owners buy a dog DNA test once, usually when they wonder about a mixed breed dog, then tell friends the result.
So the sale is won in the first line, where the owner decides the question about their own dog is theirs.
Your 13 of 22 copy ads open on the same “ever look at your dog” question, so test three new openers built from your product.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 16 Oct 2026
points: 13 of 22 copy ads open on the same “ever look at your dog” question, so one pitch repeats across the account. Test three new openers: the exact breed mix from 400+ breeds, the 270+ condition screen, and their DNA traits.

The site shows prices from $29.99 to $139, yet 0 of 30 ads mention price, so buyers click without seeing a cost. Print the breed and health kit price on one creative beside the breed ID kit and test it.
One exact copy runs in 13 of 22 ads, so a buyer who sees one sees them all. Keep the copy, rewrite the opening line, and change the creative in each of those 13 runs, starting with the video.

None of your 30 ads carries a proof number, so a new buyer gets breed claims with nothing to check them against. Confirm one current number, like a review count, and open two ads with it on the creative.

ads_1: New breed and health openers tested against the current dog question
soc_1: Brand social strategy across Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube
